overview: The City Council approved a six-year wage agreement for police unions and ordained the creation of a municipal Tree Committee. They also set the fiscal year 2026 property tax rates, maintaining a split rate while declining to adopt residential or small commercial exemptions.

items.title: Meeting Records and Routine Procedural Matters
items.summary: Approved the regular meeting records from November 12, 2025.

items.title: Resolution for George Sacco
items.summary: Passed a resolution expressing condolences for the passing of former School Committee member and State Representative George Sacco.

items.title: Police Patrol and Superiors Wage Adjustments
items.summary: Approved a six-year contract for the Police Patrol and Police Superiors unions through 2028, which includes annual wage increases for cost-of-living adjustments and body-worn camera implementation.

items.title: Business Licenses and Grants of Location
items.summary: Approved extended operating hours for Raza's Grill and granted locations for National Grid to install utility equipment on Bradbury Avenue and Ross Street.

items.title: Salem Street Zoning Corridor Map Change
items.summary: Continued the public hearing on proposed Salem Street zoning map changes to December 2nd following an extensive debate regarding the Mayor's funding conditions for future rezoning phases. Councilors requested a clear public commitment from the Mayor regarding the resources allocated for community engagement and communications before taking a final vote.

items.title: FY 2026 Property Tax Classification
items.summary: Adopted a residential factor of 0.905494 to maintain the split tax rate for fiscal year 2026, though the Council voted against adopting residential and small commercial exemptions. The body also referred a discussion on funding for additional assessing department staff to the Committee of the Whole to explore the future feasibility of residential exemptions.

items.title: Trash Collection and Zero Waste Resolution
items.summary: Passed a resolution requesting administrative reports and a public forum regarding the newly announced shift to bi-weekly trash collection starting in 2027. Councilors expressed significant concern over the rollout of the initiative and requested specific mitigation strategies for rodent control and impacts on high-density neighborhoods.

items.title: Tree Committee Ordinance
items.summary: Ordained an ordinance establishing a volunteer Tree Committee to assist the city warden with planting reports, tree hearings, and public education efforts.
